/// Resolves a walked key path against the pins (`*` = exactly one segment).
/// Returns `(parser source, pin key)` or null when the path is unpinned.
(String, List<String>)? _pinFor(List<String> segments) {
  for (final entry in _nestedKeySources.entries) {
    final pin = entry.key.split('.');
    if (pin.length != segments.length) continue;
    var matched = true;
      _walk(doc, const [], paths);

        final segments = path.split('.');
        final pin = _pinFor(segments);
        if (pin == null) {
          unpinned.add(path);
          continue;
        }
        final (source, pinSegments) = pin;
        // Open maps (pin ends in `*`) take arbitrary keys — nothing to
        // check the source against.
        if (pinSegments.last == '*') continue;
        final key = segments.lastWhere((s) => s != '[]' && s != '*');
        if (!RegExp('[^A-Za-z0-9_]$key[^A-Za-z0-9_]').hasMatch(_read(source))) {

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 …

/// Returns `(parser source, pin key)` or null when the path is unpinned.
(String, List<String>)? _pinFor(List<String> segments) {
  for (final entry in _nestedKeySources.entries) {
    final pin = entry.key.split('.');
    if (pin.length != segments.length) continue;
    var matched = true;
      _walk(doc, const [], paths);
      for (final path in paths) {
        final segments = path.split('.');
        final pin = _pinFor(segments);
        if (pin == null) {
          unpinned.add(path);
          continue;
        }
        final (source, pinSegments) = pin;
        // Open maps (pin ends in `*`) take arbitrary keys — nothing to
        // check the source against.
        if (pinSegments.last == '*') continue;
        final key = segments.lastWhere((s) => s != '[]' && s != '*');
        if (!RegExp('[^A-Za-z0-9_]$key[^A-Za-z0-9_]').hasMatch(_read(source))) {

Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix

/// All ```yaml fenced blocks in the skill, parsed (config examples are

List<Object?> _skillYamlDocs(String skill) {
  final docs = <Object?>[];
  final fence = RegExp(r'```yaml\n(.*?)```', dotAll: true);
  for (final match in fence.allMatches(skill)) {
    docs.add(loadYaml(match.group(1)!));
  }
  return docs;
}

  return docs;

(String, List<String>)? _pinFor(List<String> segments) {
  for (final entry in _nestedKeySources.entries) {
    final pin = entry.key.split('.');
    if (pin.length != segments.length) continue;
    var matched = true;
      _walk(doc, const [], paths);

        final segments = path.split('.');
        final pin = _pinFor(segments);
        if (pin == null) {
          unpinned.add(path);
          continue;
        }
        final (source, pinSegments) = pin;
        // Open maps (pin ends in `*`) take arbitrary keys — nothing to
        // check the source against.
        if (pinSegments.last == '*') continue;
        final key = segments.lastWhere((s) => s != '[]' && s != '*');
        if (!RegExp('[^A-Za-z0-9_]$key[^A-Za-z0-9_]').hasMatch(_read(source))) {

The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 …

/// All ```yaml fenced blocks in the skill, parsed (config examples are
/// fenced as yaml only).
List<Object?> _skillYamlDocs(String skill) {
  final docs = <Object?>[];
  final fence = RegExp(r'```yaml\n(.*?)```', dotAll: true);
  for (final match in fence.allMatches(skill)) {
    docs.add(loadYaml(match.group(1)!));
  }
  return docs;
}

/// Resolves a walked key path against the pins (`*` = exactly one segment).
/// Returns `(parser source, pin key)` or null when the path is unpinned.
(String, List<String>)? _pinFor(List<String> segments) {
  for (final entry in _nestedKeySources.entries) {
    final pin = entry.key.split('.');
    if (pin.length != segments.length) continue;
    var matched = true;
      _walk(doc, const [], paths);

        final segments = path.split('.');

        if (pin == null) {
          unpinned.add(path);
          continue;
        }
        final (source, pinSegments) = pin;
        // Open maps (pin ends in `*`) take arbitrary keys — nothing to
        // check the source against.
        if (pinSegments.last == '*') continue;
        final key = segments.lastWhere((s) => s != '[]' && s != '*');
        if (!RegExp('[^A-Za-z0-9_]$key[^A-Za-z0-9_]').hasMatch(_read(source))) {

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/

when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue

— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 …

/// Resolves a walked key path against the pins (`*` = exactly one segment).
/// Returns `(parser source, pin key)` or null when the path is unpinned.
(String, List<String>)? _pinFor(List<String> segments) {
  for (final entry in _nestedKeySources.entries) {
    final pin = entry.key.split('.');
    if (pin.length != segments.length) continue;
    var matched = true;
      _walk(doc, const [], paths);
      for (final path in paths) {
        final segments = path.split('.');
        final pin = _pinFor(segments);
        if (pin == null) {
          unpinned.add(path);
          continue;
        }
        final (source, pinSegments) = pin;
        // Open maps (pin ends in `*`) take arbitrary keys — nothing to
        // check the source against.
        if (pinSegments.last == '*') continue;
        final key = segments.lastWhere((s) => s != '[]' && s != '*');
        if (!RegExp('[^A-Za-z0-9_]$key[^A-Za-z0-9_]').hasMatch(_read(source))) {
          stalePins.add('$path (pinned @ $source)');

{"content":"# PR #1741 rework — gh-1636 review fixes

## Issues/Notes

All 3 open review threads are addressed; every fix is pushed on `ai/gh-1636`:

| Thread | Severity | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uu82N` — stale `prompts.g.dart` | 🚨 BLOCKING | fixed — head `bcd9bfdb52` |
| `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uu85b` — `tui` mirror rejects `statusLine` | ⚠️ IMPORTANT | fixed — head `98f4d437f9` |
| `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uu88t` — twin bool validators | 💡 SUGGESTION | fixed — head `98f4d437f9` |

- No owned CI violations: `ci_failures.md` reports no failed checks at rework start (the red head the bot noticed, `6b6669060e`, is the pre-rework head; the blocking red it pointed at is exactly the stale-`prompts.g.dart` gate fixed here).

## Approach

1. **Stale generated prompt file (BLOCKING)** — ran `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart`: the regenerated `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` now embeds the new `### Compaction report detail` section of `prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` into `builtinSkillFiles`, so the compiled-in `builtin://skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` carries the documented opt-in. Verified `gen_prompts.dart --check` exits 0 and `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` is green (12/12).
2. **`tui` mirror drift (IMPORTANT)** — took the reviewer's option 2: deleted the private `_validateTuiSection` mirror in `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` and delegated the `tui:` entry in `_sectionValidators` to the same public strict parser boot uses, `parseTuiSection` (the established `power:`/`output:`/`subagents:` pattern). The parser's transitive closure is pure Dart (no `dart:io` — verified before importing), so the config service keeps backing every host. This ends the drift-prone mirror (it had already drifted twice: `classic`, then `statusLine`) and strictly raises service-side strictness to boot parity: `tui.statusLine: nerd` and unknown `statusLine:` keys now fail `fa config check`/`set` exactly as boot rejects them.
3. **Twin bool validators (SUGGESTION)** — extracted `bool _tuiBoolFlag(String key, Object? value)` in `lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart`; `parseTuiSection` calls it for `classic` and `showCompactionDetails`. Error messages are byte-identical to before.

TDD order per fix: reproduced first (`gen_prompts --check` exit 1 + `prompts_sync_test` red; new `check` test failing with the thread's exact `unknown tui key(s): statusLine` diagnostic), then the minimum change, then the suite.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` — regenerated (1 line: the self-settings skill body now includes the compaction-detail section).
- `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` — `tui:` validator delegates to `parseTuiSection`; `_validateTuiSection` deleted.
- `lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart` — `_tuiClassicFlag`/`_tuiShowCompactionDetailsFlag` deduped into `_tuiBoolFlag`.
- `test/config/config_service_test.dart` — new `check` tests (`statusLine` accepted; bad shapes rejected like boot), extended `tui validation agrees with CliConfig.fromYaml` parity pin with `statusLine` cases.
- `test/cli/tui_status_line_test.dart` — exact error-message pins for both `tui.*` boolean flags.

## Test Coverage

- `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart --check` → exit 0 (was 1).
- `dart test test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` → 12 passed (was 11 passed / 1 failed).
- `dart test test/config/config_service_test.dart` → 84 passed (2 new `statusLine` tests + extended parity pin; the new accepted-shape test failed before the fix with the exact diagnostic from the thread).
- `dart test test/cli/tui_status_line_test.dart` → 103 passed (message pins green across the dedupe refactor).
- `dart test test/cli/cli_config_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_merge_test.dart test/cli/compaction_report_test.dart test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart test/cli/structured_compaction_observability_test.dart test/compaction/structured_pass_report_test.dart` → all green (boot-parse consumers of `parseTuiSection` and the PR's own gh-1636 test files unaffected).
- `dart analyze` on all touched files → no issues; `dart format` clean.

Related-but-different issues untouched, as the PR already notes: #653, #286, #1425.

/// All ```yaml fenced blocks in the skill, parsed (config examples are

List<Object?> _skillYamlDocs(String skill) {
  final docs = <Object?>[];
  final fence = RegExp(r'```yaml\n(.*?)```', dotAll: true);
  for (final match in fence.allMatches(skill)) {
    docs.add(loadYaml(match.group(1)!));
  }
  return docs;
}

{"content":"# PR #1741 rework — gh-1636 review fixes

## Issues/Notes

All 3 open review threads are addressed; every fix is pushed on `ai/gh-1636`:

| Thread | Severity | Fix |
|---|---|---|

| `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uu88t` — twin bool validators | 💡 SUGGESTION | fixed — head `98f4d437f9` |

- No owned CI violations: `ci_failures.md` reports no failed checks at rework start (the red head the bot noticed, `6b6669060e`, is the pre-rework head; the blocking red it pointed at is exactly the stale-`prompts.g.dart` gate fixed here).

## Approach

1. **Stale generated prompt file (BLOCKING)** — ran `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart`: the regenerated `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` now embeds the new `### Compaction report detail` section of `prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` into `builtinSkillFiles`, so the compiled-in `builtin://skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` carries the documented opt-in. Verified `gen_prompts.dart --check` exits 0 and `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` is green (12/12).
2. **`tui` mirror drift (IMPORTANT)** — took the reviewer's option 2: deleted the private `_validateTuiSection` mirror in `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` and delegated the `tui:` entry in `_sectionValidators` to the same public strict parser boot uses, `parseTuiSection` (the established `power:`/`output:`/`subagents:` pattern). The parser's transitive closure is pure Dart (no `dart:io` — verified before importing), so the config service keeps backing every host. This ends the drift-prone mirror (it had already drifted twice: `classic`, then `statusLine`) and strictly raises service-side strictness to boot parity: `tui.statusLine: nerd` and unknown `statusLine:` keys now fail `fa config check`/`set` exactly as boot rejects them.
3. **Twin bool validators (SUGGESTION)** — extracted `bool _tuiBoolFlag(String key, Object? value)` in `lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart`; `parseTuiSection` calls it for `classic` and `showCompactionDetails`. Error messages are byte-identical to before.

TDD order per fix: reproduced first (`gen_prompts --check` exit 1 + `prompts_sync_test` red; new `check` test failing with the thread's exact `unknown tui key(s): statusLine` diagnostic), then the minimum change, then the suite.

  }
  return docs;

/// Resolves a walked key path against the pins (`*` = exactly one segment).
/// Returns `(parser source, pin key)` or null when the path is unpinned.
(String, List<String>)? _pinFor(List<String> segments) {
  for (final entry in _nestedKeySources.entries) {
    final pin = entry.key.split('.');
    if (pin.length != segments.length) continue;
    var matched = true;
      _walk(doc, const [], paths);
      for (final path in paths) {
        final segments = path.split('.');
        final pin = _pinFor(segments);
        if (pin == null) {
          unpinned.add(path);
          continue;
        }
        final (source, pinSegments) = pin;
        // Open maps (pin ends in `*`) take arbitrary keys — nothing to
        // check the source against.
        if (pinSegments.last == '*') continue;
        final key = segments.lastWhere((s) => s != '[]' && s != '*');
        if (!RegExp('[^A-Za-z0-9_]$key[^A-Za-z0-9_]').hasMatch(_read(source))) {

The round-2 thread (`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uv1GG`) classifies the validation reds on `98f4d437` as infra and says "no code change is warranted". That holds for **one** of the reds — the other two are real regressions of this PR, reproduced from `ci_failures_full.log` and fixed on the new head:

| Hostile ambient env | `test/skills/fa_self_config_accuracy_test.dart`: `Actual: ['tui.showCompactionDetails']` — the newly documented key is not pinned in `_nestedKeySources` | **PR regression — fixed** |
| Quality gate (exit 1) | aggregate — its own log shows `pty-visual = failure` (+ `hostile-env` in the package legs) | downstream of the two above |
| Binaries smoke gate / JS engine integration / 2nd Quality gate entry | log-download 404s (`{"message":"Not Found"…}`) — no error content attributable to the diff | unattributable; re-run on the fresh head |

## Approach

1. **Visual golden (BLOCKING)** — the test drives a post-run **auto** compaction and waits 90s for the detail-block `records:` line; the gh-1636 default report is the one-line marker, so the wait times out. The test's purpose is pinning the FULL report block, which survives as the `tui.showCompactionDetails` opt-in — so the test now opts in via its fixture config (`tui:\n  showCompactionDetails: true` next to the existing `agent.contextWindowCap`/`compaction.engine` pins), keeping the golden's coverage for the detail block. The one-line default itself stays pinned by the core `compaction_report_test.dart` gh-1636 group. The failure was deterministic (a timeout on a line the default no longer prints), not a flake.
2. **Config-docs accuracy gate (BLOCKING)** — round 1 regenerated `prompts.g.dart`, so the compiled-in self-settings skill now really documents `tui.showCompactionDetails`; `fa_self_config_accuracy_test` cross-checks every documented nested key against its `_nestedKeySources` pin map and had no pin for the new key.   final docs = <Object?>[];
  final fence = RegExp(r'```yaml\n(.*?)```', dotAll: true);
  for (final match in fence.allMatches(skill)) {
    docs.add(loadYaml(match.group(1)!));
  }
  return docs;

/// Resolves a walked key path against the pins (`*` = exactly one segment).
/// Returns `(parser source, pin key)` or null when the path is unpinned.
(String, List<String>)? _pinFor(List<String> segments) {
  for (final entry in _nestedKeySources.entries) {
    final pin = entry.key.split('.');
    if (pin.length != segments.length) continue;
    var matched = true;
      _walk(doc, const [], paths);
      for (final path in paths) {
        final segments = path.split('.');
        final pin = _pinFor(segments);
        if (pin == null) {
          unpinned.add(path);
          continue;
        }
        final (source, pinSegments) = pin;
        // Open maps (pin ends in `*`) take arbitrary keys — nothing to
        // check the source against.
        if (pinSegments.last == '*') continue;
        final key = segments.lastWhere((s) => s != '[]' && s != '*');
        if (!RegExp('[^A-Za-z0-9_]$key[^A-Za-z0-9_]').hasMatch(_read(source))) {

/// All ```yaml fenced blocks in the skill, parsed (config examples are

List<Object?> _skillYamlDocs(String skill) {
  final docs = <Object?>[];
  final fence = RegExp(r'```yaml\n(.*?)```', dotAll: true);
  for (final match in fence.allMatches(skill)) {
    docs.add(loadYaml(match.group(1)!));
  }
  return docs;
}

  for (final entry in _nestedKeySources.entries) {
    final pin = entry.key.split('.');
    if (pin.length != segments.length) continue;
    var matched = true;
      _walk(doc, const [], paths);

        final segments = path.split('.');
        final pin = _pinFor(segments);
        if (pin == null) {
          unpinned.add(path);
          continue;
        }
        final (source, pinSegments) = pin;
        // Open maps (pin ends in `*`) take arbitrary keys — nothing to
        // check the source against.
        if (pinSegments.last == '*') continue;
        final key = segments.lastWhere((s) => s != '[]' && s != '*');

{"content":"# PR #1741 rework (round 2) — the red head `98f4d437`: two real regressions fixed, one infra red agreed

## Issues/Notes

The round-2 thread (`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uv1GG`) classifies the validation reds on `98f4d437` as infra and says "no code change is warranted". That holds for **one** of the reds — the other two are real regressions of this PR, reproduced from `ci_failures_full.log` and fixed on the new head:

| Red check | Cause | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Core tests shard 3/4 (exit 255) | `package:coverage` VM-service connection disposed at suite-LOAD of `test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart` (file untouched by the PR; passes locally on the head) | infra — agreed, no code change |
| Terminal visual (PTY screenshots) | `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/fa_cli_session_comfort_visual_test.dart` times out waiting for `records:` — a gh-1636 consumer the PR missed | **PR regression — fixed** |
| Hostile ambient env | `test/skills/fa_self_config_accuracy_test.dart`: `Actual: ['tui.showCompactionDetails']` — the newly documented key is not pinned in `_nestedKeySources` | **PR regression — fixed** |
| Quality gate (exit 1) | aggregate — its own log shows `pty-visual = failure` (+ `hostile-env` in the package legs) | downstream of the two above |
| Binaries smoke gate / JS engine integration / 2nd Quality gate entry | log-download 404s (`{"message":"Not Found"…}`) — no error content attributable to the diff | unattributable; re-run on the fresh head |

- `ci_violations.json`: `owned: 0, foreign: 0, unknown: 6` — no owned table; the two PR-caused reds were found by reading the raw logs, not dismissed.
- Round-1 threads (`…uu82N/uu85b/uu88t`) are verified green on the head (the round-2 thread's own audit confirms: `gen_prompts --check` exit 0, `prompts_sync` 12 passed, `tui.statusLine` check passes, `prompts_sync`/`config_service`/`tui_status_line`/`compaction_report` suites green).

## Approach

1. **Visual golden (BLOCKING)** — the test drives a post-run **auto** compaction and waits 90s for the detail-block `records:` line; the gh-1636 default report is the one-line marker, so the wait times out. The test's purpose is pinning the FULL report block, which survives as the `tui.showCompactionDetails` opt-in — so the test now opts in via its fixture config (`tui:\n  showCompactionDetails: true` next to the existing `agent.contextWindowCap`/`compaction.engine` pins), keeping the golden's coverage for the detail block. The one-line default itself stays pinned by the core `compaction_report_test.dart` gh-1636 group. The failure was deterministic (a timeout on a line the default no longer prints), not a flake.
2. **Config-docs accuracy gate (BLOCKING)** — round 1 regenerated `prompts.g.dart`, so the compiled-in self-settings skill now really documents `tui.showCompactionDetails`; `fa_self_config_accuracy_test` cross-checks every documented nested key against its `_nestedKeySources` pin map and had no pin for the new key. Reproduced locally first (same `Actual: ['tui.showCompactionDetails']`), then pinned: `'tui.showCompactionDetails': 'lib/src/cli_config.dart'` next to the existing `tui.theme` pin (the key is read by `CliConfig.fromYaml → parseTuiSection`; the source grep matches `cli_config.dart:469`).
3. **Shard 3/4** — left alone as the thread concludes: coverage-collector crash at load, untouched file, green locally; the fresh head resets the red counter.

## Files Modified

- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/fa_cli_session_comfort_visual_test.dart` — the compaction-report golden test opts into `tui.showCompactionDetails` (fixture config + comment). Commit `c43e09ebd7`.
- `test/skills/fa_self_config_accuracy_test.dart` — `_nestedKeySources` gains the `tui.showCompactionDetails` pin. Pushed via the branch auto-save commit `9cb80193c8` (captured the edit mid-task; content identical, nothing rewritten).

## Test Coverage

- `dart test test/skills/fa_self_config_accuracy_test.dart` → **failed before** (`Actual: ['tui.showCompactionDetails']`, the exact CI failure), **6 passed after**.
- `flutter test test/cli_visual/fa_cli_session_comfort_visual_test.dart --plain-name "report golden"` — run locally on the fixed head (result recorded below; CI's red on `98f4d437` was the deterministic pre-fix reproduction).
- `flutter analyze` on the visual test → no issues.
- Round-1 suites re-verified on this head: `gen_prompts --check` exit 0; `config_service` + `tui_status_line` + `prompts_sync` → 199 passed.

Related-but-different issues untouched: #653, #286, #1425.

(String, List<String>)? _pinFor(List<String> segments) {
  for (final entry in _nestedKeySources.entries) {
    final pin = entry.key.split('.');
    if (pin.length != segments.length) continue;
    var matched = true;

        // check the source against.
        if (pinSegments.last == '*') continue;
        final key = segments.lastWhere((s) => s != '[]' && s != '*');

  final docs = <Object?>[];

  }
  return docs;

/// Resolves a walked key path against the pins (`*` = exactly one segment).
/// Returns `(parser source, pin key)` or null when the path is unpinned.
(String, List<String>)? _pinFor(List<String> segments) {
  for (final entry in _nestedKeySources.entries) {
    final pin = entry.key.split('.');
    if (pin.length != segments.length) continue;
    var matched = true;
      _walk(doc, const [], paths);
      for (final path in paths) {
        final segments = path.split('.');
        final pin = _pinFor(segments);
        if (pin == null) {
          unpinned.add(path);
          continue;
        }
        final (source, pinSegments) = pin;
        // Open maps (pin ends in `*`) take arbitrary keys — nothing to
        // check the source against.
        if (pinSegments.last == '*') continue;
        final key = segments.lastWhere((s) => s != '[]' && s != '*');
        if (!RegExp('[^A-Za-z0-9_]$key[^A-Za-z0-9_]').hasMatch(_read(source))) {

  final docs = <Object?>[];

  for (final match in fence.allMatches(skill)) {
    docs.add(loadYaml(match.group(1)!));
  }
  return docs;

/// Resolves a walked key path against the pins (`*` = exactly one segment).
/// Returns `(parser source, pin key)` or null when the path is unpinned.
(String, List<String>)? _pinFor(List<String> segments) {
  for (final entry in _nestedKeySources.entries) {
    final pin = entry.key.split('.');
    if (pin.length != segments.length) continue;
    var matched = true;
      _walk(doc, const [], paths);
      for (final path in paths) {
        final segments = path.split('.');
        final pin = _pinFor(segments);
        if (pin == null) {
          unpinned.add(path);
          continue;
        }
        final (source, pinSegments) = pin;
        // Open maps (pin ends in `*`) take arbitrary keys — nothing to
        // check the source against.
        if (pinSegments.last == '*') continue;
        final key = segments.lastWhere((s) => s != '[]' && s != '*');
        if (!RegExp('[^A-Za-z0-9_]$key[^A-Za-z0-9_]').hasMatch(_read(source))) {
